orient: Establish the person's current question and current authorization from this conversation. Read the generated briefing, relevant saved corrections and a useful account bundle. Build a provisional context map: roles, periods, work episodes, relationships and important gaps. Identify what is known, uncertain and worth investigating. Do not force a career narrative or begin with a full adversarial challenge. Address any known factual conflict immediately. Save concise findings and consequential leads, then continue the next useful round without asking the person to prompt you again.
investigate: Choose the consequential ready lead that could most change the context map; the saved order is a suggestion, not a quota. Form a focused question and inspect authorized original records with surrounding context. Split multi-part questions and follow relevant account links. Check ownership, action state, chronology, adoption, outcomes or personal meaning as relevant. Revisit the context map after each round: what belongs together, what needs separating, what new context is missing? Address contradictions when found; a later full challenge is no reason to defer them. Save what changed or stayed unchanged, exact record links and revised leads. Then call next again and continue while useful authorized work remains.
map: Revisit the whole context map in the current scope before a full challenge. Compare the provisional map with what the research rounds actually established: roles, dates, episode boundaries, shared work, connections and the person's own meaning. Read adjacent authorized context when it could change this picture. Do not mistake no saved leads for complete understanding. Create ready leads for consequential accessible gaps and iterate; keep blocked questions explicit without stopping unrelated work. Save a concise map finding with exact record links explaining what changed, what remains unknown and why the map is ready for challenge if no useful accessible lead remains. No fixed number of rounds is required. A map finding is an interpretation, never new evidence, permission or the person's approval. Then call next again.
challenge: After building and revisiting the context map, challenge its strongest material claims before handing it back. Try to disprove them, look for contrary evidence, missing shared credit, proposals presented as delivery, adoption presented as impact, and unsupported causal links. Reuse sufficient originals; search again only when a consequential accessible lead remains. A challenge may narrow a claim without adding detail. Record the finding and any new leads, then call next again; new leads return to research and map revision. Do not fabricate activity to satisfy a pass count.
reconcile: The evidence or the person's review input changed since the saved investigation. Read the supplied new review input and compare affected accounts, originals, corrections and prior findings. Preserve earlier notes as historical work; reopen only relevant conclusions and leads. Do not merely refresh fingerprints. Incorporate supported changes, retain uncertain self-reports and reuse existing source/claim IDs. Bind the revised investigation to contextSha256 and reviewSha256 from the current generated view after actual reconciliation, record the result and continue the next useful round.
handoff: Check the recorded stopping reason against the actual remaining work. If a consequential authorized lead remains, reopen it and continue. Otherwise save the current draft, exact unresolved questions and the next conditional action. Ask only what the person can supply or authorize and only when it matters. A blocked question does not block unrelated work. Do not mark the person as having reviewed the result. This foreground run cannot schedule itself or continue after the host ends it.
